requirements.title: An ERRMSG variable is independent of allocation actions, allocate-object properties, and STAT value
requirements.definition: The errmsg-variable shall not be an allocate-object of the ALLOCATE or DEALLOCATE statement in which it appears. Its denotation shall not depend on the value, bounds, deferred type parameters, allocation status, or association status of any allocate-object in that statement, and shall not depend on the value of the stat-variable. The scalar default character variable form for ERRMSG= is owned by 9.7.1.1 R931 for ALLOCATE and by the corresponding DEALLOCATE syntax owner; this requirement owns the shared independence restriction.

pending.errmsg-variable-not-allocate-object: PENDING diagnostic-policy/control source: attempt ALLOCATE(msg, ERRMSG=msg, STAT=s) where msg is a deferred-length default CHARACTER allocatable and otherwise satisfies the ERRMSG variable form; repair by using a separate fixed-length default CHARACTER variable emsg and observe s==0, ALLOCATED(msg), LEN(msg), and assigned literal content. Invalidity is attributable to S9.7.5-001 rather than R931.
pending.errmsg-variable-not-deallocate-object: PENDING diagnostic-policy/control source: allocate a default CHARACTER allocatable msg, then attempt DEALLOCATE(msg, ERRMSG=msg, STAT=s); repair by using a separate ERRMSG variable emsg and observe s==0 and ALLOCATED(msg)==.FALSE. DEALLOCATE syntax and deallocation effects remain 9.7.3 dependencies.
pending.no-errmsg-value-dependence-on-allocate-o: PENDING diagnostic-policy/control source: use an ERRMSG variable designator such as emsg(f(x)) where f references the current value of allocate-object x in the same ALLOCATE or DEALLOCATE statement; repair by computing the subscript from an independent literal before the statement and observe STAT zero plus a literal object result. No undefined allocate-object value is read.
pending.no-errmsg-bounds-dependence-on-allocate-: PENDING diagnostic-policy/control source: select ERRMSG=emsg(UBOUND(a,1)) or equivalent where the ERRMSG variable designator depends on bounds of a same-statement allocate-object; repair by using an independent literal subscript and observe STAT zero plus allocation/deallocation status. Invalidity is attributed to S9.7.5-001, not array bounds syntax.
pending.no-errmsg-deferred-type-parameter-depend: PENDING diagnostic-policy/control source: make the ERRMSG variable designator depend on LEN or another deferred type parameter of a same-statement character or parameterized allocate-object; repair by using an independent length value and observe STAT zero plus a literal. Type parameter ownership stays in the declaration and allocation subclauses.
pending.no-errmsg-allocation-status-dependence-o: PENDING diagnostic-policy/control source: select the ERRMSG variable using ALLOCATED(a) for an allocatable allocate-object a in the same statement; repair by saving the inquiry result before the statement and observe STAT zero plus allowed allocation status. Runtime detectability is limited and no required static diagnostic is claimed.
pending.no-errmsg-association-status-dependence-: PENDING diagnostic-policy/control source: select the ERRMSG variable using ASSOCIATED(p) for a pointer allocate-object p in the same statement; repair by evaluating the inquiry only when pointer association status is defined before the statement and observe STAT zero plus ASSOCIATED(p). The plan must not query undefined association status.
pending.no-errmsg-stat-value-dependence: PENDING diagnostic-policy/control source: use an ERRMSG variable designator whose subscript or component selection depends on the value of the STAT variable in the same statement; repair by using an independent literal selector and observe STAT zero plus successful allocation/deallocation. Invalidity is attributed to S9.7.5-001, not to R946 or R931 variable form.

requirements.oracle: All facets are explicit PENDING source plans. Positive controls use independent literal values, portable inquiry results, ALLOCATED/ASSOCIATED/STAT/ERRMSG observations after establishing that the statement executed, or separately gated multi-image observations. Negative plans use an otherwise conforming source and a minimal repair, with invalidity attributed to the named requirement rather than to ALLOCATE syntax, DEALLOCATE syntax, stat-variable typing, errmsg-variable typing, undefined storage, compiler agreement, addresses, TRANSFER, emitted code, or deliberate resource exhaustion.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This is a source-only catalogue. It creates no Fortran test program, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. The p1 shall-not restrictions are not numbered constraints; the diagnostic obligation is not-required even where an implementation might reject a particular source form. Dependence tests need independent review so a negative is not actually caused by invalid variable designator syntax or unsafe inquiry of undefined allocation or association status.

requirements.title: ERRMSG assignment occurs on ALLOCATE or DEALLOCATE error and is unchanged on success
requirements.definition: If an error condition occurs during execution of an ALLOCATE or DEALLOCATE statement with an ERRMSG= specifier, the errmsg-variable is assigned an explanatory message as if by intrinsic assignment. If no such error condition occurs, the definition status and value of the errmsg-variable are unchanged. The exact explanatory message content is processor dependent or otherwise not specified by this subclause; this requirement owns only assignment on error and unchanged definition status and value on success.

pending.allocate-error-errmsg-assigned: PENDING source-classification plan only: a deterministic standard-specified ALLOCATE error, such as allocating an already allocated allocatable object with STAT=s and ERRMSG=msg, can establish the error premise and nonzero STAT under 9.7.4, but 9.7.5 p2 does not specify the explanatory message content. Therefore no portable value comparison, including inequality with a chosen sentinel, can establish that the ERRMSG assignment occurred; a future fixture would need a separately justified processor-specific premise and must not use resource exhaustion.
pending.deallocate-error-errmsg-assigned: PENDING source-classification plan only: the deterministic standard-specified DEALLOCATE error from 9.7.3.2 p1 can establish the error premise and nonzero STAT under 9.7.4, but 9.7.5 p2 does not specify the explanatory message content. Therefore no portable value comparison, including inequality with a chosen sentinel, can establish that the ERRMSG assignment occurred; a future fixture would need a separately justified processor-specific premise, with a repaired success control that allocates first and observes STAT zero.
pending.errmsg-assignment-as-intrinsic-assignmen: PENDING source-classification plan only: although p2 says the explanatory message is assigned as if by intrinsic assignment, the assigned character content is unspecified. Without a separately justified processor-specific premise about that content, no portable comparison to a literal, no inequality with a sentinel, and no padding or truncation observation can prove the intrinsic-assignment effect occurred.
pending.allocate-success-errmsg-defined-value-un: PENDING complete source: initialize fixed-length default CHARACTER msg to literal 'alloc-ok-sentinel', execute successful ALLOCATE(x, STAT=s, ERRMSG=msg), and observe s==0, ALLOCATED(x), x assigned literal 751, and msg still equal to the sentinel. This tests the no-error value-unchanged branch for a defined errmsg-variable.
pending.deallocate-success-errmsg-defined-value-: PENDING complete source: initialize fixed-length default CHARACTER msg to literal 'dealloc-ok-sentinel', successfully DEALLOCATE an allocated object with STAT=s and ERRMSG=msg, then observe s==0, ALLOCATED false, and msg still equal to the sentinel. DEALLOCATE semantics are dependencies.
pending.success-errmsg-undefined-status-unchange: PENDING source-classification plan only: the source says definition status is unchanged when no error occurs, including an initially undefined errmsg-variable, but a conforming executable oracle cannot read undefined character storage to prove unchanged undefined status. This facet remains pending until the suite has an approved definition-status oracle that does not inspect undefined storage; no literal value check is proposed for the undefined case.

review_rationale: Independent source review in doc/source_audits/batch_096.json reads both original 9.7.5 units in full and confirms the ERRMSG= specifier: p1 keeps every independence restriction on the errmsg-variable, and p2 separates the two asymmetric directions. On error the variable is assigned an explanatory message as if by intrinsic assignment, but the message content is unspecified, so the reviewer correctly rejected an oracle that inferred assignment from inequality with a chosen sentinel; those facets are now classification-only and record that a future fixture needs a separately justified processor-specific premise. When no error occurs the definition status and value are unchanged, which is portably observable, so the success facets retain real plans that preset a sentinel and assert it is unchanged after a successful statement. The initially undefined branch stays classification-only because a conforming program cannot read undefined storage. All14 facets remain pending source plans; no case, execution, oracle or fixture approval is created.
